phys-opt-01-c2.text: Florida State University, Optical Microscopy Primer (Optical Society of America: Exploring the Science of Light). Color and Light. Florida State University Molecular Expressions / OSA.
phys-opt-01-c2.quote: The range of wavelengths (400 - 700 nm) of visible light is centrally located in the electromagnetic spectrum (Fig. 1).
phys-opt-01-c2.claim: Visible light spans roughly 400 nm (violet) to 700 nm (red)

phys-opt-01-c3.text: Samuel J. Ling, Jeff Sanny, William Moebs (OpenStax) (2016). University Physics Volume 3, 6.2 Photoelectric Effect. OpenStax, Rice University.
phys-opt-01-c3.quote: The photoelectric effect was explained in 1905 by A. Einstein.
phys-opt-01-c3.claim: The photoelectric effect (Einstein 1905) showed that low-frequency light can't eject electrons no matter how bright it is, because each photon must individually have enough energy.
